summary: Retest of the 2 minor fixes from iteration 7 on the preview URL. All 4 requested scenarios PASS. (1) With lockout at now+20s and attempts=5, the 'Account Locked' panel shows and the form is hidden. Without a reload, the password form appeared after 30.4s, localStorage admin_lockout was removed and admin_attempts was set to '0', and the form shows '5 attempts remaining'. (2) With lockout at now+70s, the countdown read 'Try again in 2 minutes' at first and changed to '1 minutes' after 16s, with no reload. (3) Backend: 5 rapid POST /api/admin/login with the same X-Forwarded-For returned 401, and the 6th returned 429. A different X-Forwarded-For then got 401. ETIadmin@2026 returned 200 with requires_setup=true. (4) Regression: with an expired lockout and a wrong password, the page shows '4 attempts remaining' and localStorage attempts=1. The correct password reaches the Set Up 2FA screen with the QR code and secret. 2FA setup was NOT completed. New security finding: the client controls X-Forwarded-For, so changing it on every request bypasses the admin login rate limit completely.

minor.issue: The rate limit can be bypassed by spoofing headers. client_ip() trusts the FIRST X-Forwarded-For value, and the client can set that value (the ingress appends to it and does not overwrite it). 8 rapid requests with a different X-Forwarded-For each (198.51.100.1-8) all returned 401 and none returned 429, so an attacker gets unlimited password guesses. In contrast, requests with no header were limited correctly (429 on the 6th), and requests with a rotating X-Real-IP also got 429, so the ingress seems to overwrite X-Real-IP. Suggested fix: key only on X-Real-IP, or on the RIGHT-most / trusted-hop X-Forwarded-For entry (the one the ingress appended), not the first value. Also consider a server-side failed-attempt counter.

ui_bugs.issue: The panel unlocks up to 15s after the lockout actually expires, because of the 15s interval (a 20s lockout unlocked at about 30s). It also shows 'Try again in 1 minutes': wrong plural, and the text is coarse when under 60s remain. This is cosmetic.

issues: The 6-digit code input placeholder is cut off ('6-digit code fro') because of the wide letter-spacing

action_items: Security: change client_ip() so a spoofed client X-Forwarded-For[0] cannot bypass the 5/min admin login limit. Use X-Real-IP set by the ingress, or the last/trusted-hop XFF entry.
Optional: use a shorter tick (e.g. 1-5s), or a setTimeout set to lockoutUntil, so the panel unlocks right on time. Fix the '1 minutes' plural.
Optional: shorten the 2FA code input placeholder or reduce its letter-spacing
critical_code_review_comments: client_ip trusts the left-most X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls. This was confirmed exploitable on preview.
The lockout useEffect is correct: it clears the interval on cleanup, depends on lockoutUntil, and clears localStorage on expiry.

success_rate.backend: 100% of requested (2/2 pytest), plus 1 security finding

test_credentials: Admin password ETIadmin@2026 from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. 2FA left NOT set up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The rate limit is a fixed 5/min window. The test waits for the start of a window. Browser and curl traffic from this container share the same real IP bucket, so wait about 62s between batches. Admin 2FA is not set up in preview; do not complete setup.
rca of the issue: XFF bypass: the K8s ingress appends the real client IP to any X-Forwarded-For the client sends, so XFF[0] is whatever the attacker supplies. Repro: for i in 1..8, curl -X POST /api/admin/login -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.$i' with a wrong password. All 8 return 401 and none return 429. Mitigation: use X-Real-IP (the ingress appears to overwrite it), or XFF[-1].
